title: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer
author: Mark Twain
level: Chinese junior-high (CEFR A2-B1). Simple English meanings.

spectacles.meaning: Glasses that a person wears over the eyes to see better.

perplexed.meaning: Not sure what to think or do; mixed up.

roundabout.meaning: A short coat that fits close to the body. Boys wore it in the old days.

switch.meaning: A thin stick that bends easily. It was used to hit a child when he did wrong.

guile.meaning: Clever ways of making people believe something that is not true.

dander.meaning: Anger. In 'get my dander up', it means to become angry.

hookey.meaning: Staying away from school when you should be there. 'Play hookey' means to do this.

forestalled.meaning: Acted early to stop another person's plan from working.

knack.meaning: A natural way of doing something well and easily.

derision.meaning: Words or looks that show you think someone is silly or weak.

ambuscade.meaning: A secret attack from a place where nobody can see you. Here, Aunt Polly waits for Tom in the dark.

adamantine.meaning: Very hard and not able to be changed.

lick.meaning: To beat someone in a fight, or to hit as a way to teach a child. A 'lick' is a hit.

obleeged.meaning: A spoken form of a word that means you must do something.

whitewash.meaning: A cheap white mix of water and a white stuff. People put it on a wall to make it white.

hollow.meaning: Empty, with no real meaning or good feeling inside.

skylarking.meaning: Playing around in a loud and silly way.

taw.meaning: The big round glass ball that a player shoots at the other balls in the game.

gay.meaning: Bright and pretty, and full of fun.

waver.meaning: To begin to change your mind. You are not sure any more.

straitened.meaning: Small and not enough. Here, it is about Tom's little money and few things.

personating.meaning: Acting as if you are another person or thing.

druther.meaning: A spoken form of 'would rather'. 'You'd druther work' means 'you would rather work'.

covet.meaning: To want something very much, especially something that is another person's.

particular.meaning: Very careful and hard to please about something.

balmy.meaning: Warm and soft, in a nice way.

diluted.meaning: Made weaker by adding something. Here, she made the good words less strong.

sally.meaning: To go out quickly, as if to attack or help.

evanescent.meaning: Lasting only a very short time, then gone.

furtive.meaning: Secret and quiet, so that others will not see.

morosely.meaning: In a sad way, with a bad feeling.

beseeching.meaning: Asking in a very serious way, because you need it so much.

stealthy.meaning: Quiet and careful, so that nobody hears or sees.

deluge.meaning: A very large amount of water coming down.

tallow.meaning: Hard fat from animals. People used it to make light and to keep things dry.

audacious.meaning: Showing no fear of what other people think; very brave and rude.

benediction.meaning: Words said at the end of a church meeting, asking God to be good to the people.

scarify.meaning: To make small cuts or lines on something. Here, Tom does this to a part of the house.

counterfeited.meaning: Made to look like the real thing, so that people think it is real. Here, it is about a copy of a Barlow.

contrived.meaning: Found a way to do something, with some trouble.

disconcerted.meaning: Upset and mixed up because something went wrong.

galled.meaning: Made someone feel angry and hurt.

persuasively.meaning: In a way that tries to make a person agree.

accosted.meaning: Went up to someone and spoke to him.

waylaid.meaning: Stopped people on their way to speak to them.

reprimand.meaning: Words of anger from a person with power, because you did wrong.

superintendent.meaning: The person in charge of a school or of a church school like this one.

pulpit.meaning: A raised place in a church where the speaker stands.

pew.meaning: A long seat in a church. It is made of wood.

cravat.meaning: A wide cloth that a man wears around his neck.

mien.meaning: The way a person looks or acts.

august.meaning: Great and grand; making people feel respect.

wily.meaning: Clever, in a way that is not honest.

preposterous.meaning: So silly and wrong that nobody can believe it.

sheepish.meaning: A little sorry and low, like a person who knows he did wrong.

seductive.meaning: Very nice to think of, so that you want to go to it. Here, the summer outside pulls Tom away from church.

lavish.meaning: Giving or spending very freely; with much more than is needed.

simpering.meaning: Smiling in a silly way that is not real.

laggard.meaning: A person who is slow and comes late.

tittering.meaning: Quiet laughing that you try to keep inside.

supplication.meaning: A serious request made in a low voice, especially to God.

restive.meaning: Not able to be still, and tired of waiting.

prosy.meaning: Not interesting, because it is too long and says nothing new.

brimstone.meaning: A yellow stone that makes fire. In 'fire and brimstone' it means the fires of hell.

fillip.meaning: A quick push made with one part of the hand that is held back and then let go.

vagrant.meaning: A person who goes from place to place and has no home.

gingerly.meaning: Very careful and slow, because of fear of getting hurt.

facetious.meaning: Trying to be funny at a time when it is not the right time.

parson.meaning: A man who leads a church; a minister.

canvassed.meaning: Looked at, one part after another. Here, the boy looks at his body to find signs of sickness.

mortified.meaning: Said of a part of the body that is dead and going bad. Here, Tom says it about his foot.

expectorate.meaning: To send water from the mouth, in a rude way.

adherent.meaning: A follower; a person who stays with someone and supports him.

pariah.meaning: A person that everyone avoids and does not accept.

gaudy.meaning: With too many bright colors. Here, Tom likes Huck's wild life outside the rules.

perennial.meaning: Lasting all the time, or coming back every year.

hogshead.meaning: A very big round box for drink, made of wood.

harassed.meaning: Always troubled and pushed by other people.

spunk.meaning: In 'spunk-water', rain water in an old tree. The boys think it can take a small hard thing off the skin.

wart.meaning: A small, hard bit that grows on the skin.

ferule.meaning: A flat stick that a teacher used to hit a child on the hand.

wistfully.meaning: With a sad and longing look, wanting something you cannot easily have.

caricature.meaning: A drawing that is funny because it makes things look wrong or too big.

gable.meaning: The part of an end wall of a house that goes up to a point at the top.

portentous.meaning: Looking very big and important, as if something bad may come.

juncture.meaning: A point in time, especially an important one.

jubilant.meaning: Very happy because of a win.

botch.meaning: A job done badly. 'Made a botch of it' means did it very badly.

tick.meaning: A very small animal that bites. The boys play with one.

premature.meaning: Too early; coming before the right time.

momently.meaning: From one moment to the next; more with each moment.

deftly.meaning: In a quick and clever way, with good hands.

slathers.meaning: A very large amount of something. 'Slathers of money' means a lot of money.

repulsed.meaning: Pushed away; not allowed to come near.

andiron.meaning: A metal stand that holds wood in a fire at home.

upbraid.meaning: To say angry words to a person about what he did wrong.

baffled.meaning: Not able to find the way. Here, people thought that going across water would stop someone from following.

grisly.meaning: Very bad to look at; it makes you afraid.

doublet.meaning: A short coat that fits close to the body, worn by men long ago.

cutlass.meaning: A short, heavy, curved sword used on ships long ago.

incantation.meaning: Magic words that a person says to make something happen.

shingle.meaning: A thin flat piece of wood.

infallible.meaning: Never wrong; always certain to work.

futility.meaning: The fact that something is useless and cannot work.

caitiff.meaning: An old word for a bad man who is weak and afraid.

accoutrements.meaning: The things you carry or wear for a purpose, such as weapons and clothes.

lath.meaning: A thin, narrow piece of wood. The boys use laths as swords to play with.

doodlebug.meaning: A small animal that lives in a hole in the ground. The boys think it can answer questions.

nettle.meaning: A plant that hurts your skin when you touch it.

ensconced.meaning: Sitting in a safe place where nobody can see.

caterwauling.meaning: The loud crying that cats make at night.

deathwatch.meaning: A small animal that makes a sound like a watch in wood. People thought it meant that someone would die.

ingenuity.meaning: The power to think of clever ways to do things.

damper.meaning: Something that takes away the fun or the hope. Here, it ends the boys' talk.

pard.meaning: A short, spoken form of 'partner'; a close friend.

pallid.meaning: Very white in the face, like a sick person.

sawbones.meaning: A rude word for a doctor.

inarticulately.meaning: Without clear words; in sounds that cannot be understood.

fuddled.meaning: Not able to think well, often because of drink.

ruffian.meaning: A rough man who likes to hurt people.

apprehensively.meaning: In a worried way, afraid that something bad will happen.

tannery.meaning: A place where animal skins are worked on, to make them strong and fit to use.

verdigrease.meaning: A green stuff that grows on old metal and can make you ill.

lugubrious.meaning: Very sad and slow, in a way that seems too much.

escapade.meaning: An exciting thing to do that is against the rules.

bodings.meaning: Feelings that something bad is going to happen.

culprit.meaning: A person who did something wrong.

phase.meaning: A spoken form of a word that means to trouble or upset someone.

electrified.meaning: Made to feel a sudden, strong surprise.

ransacked.meaning: Searched very fast and roughly in every place.

ostentatiously.meaning: In a way that is made to be seen by everyone.

palsy.meaning: An illness in which the body moves without control.

miscreant.meaning: A very bad person who does bad things.

inquest.meaning: An official meeting to find out how a person died.

balefully.meaning: In a way that seems evil and full of danger.

blanched.meaning: Became white in the face, because of fear.

coroner.meaning: An officer who finds out how a person died. In the boys' game, the leader of a meeting for a dead cat, as a joke.

smuggled.meaning: Secretly took something in or out of a place.

infatuated.meaning: Filled with a strong love for something that is not good for you.

newfangled.meaning: New and strange; not liked by people who like old ways.

inveterate.meaning: Always doing the same thing, for a long time, and not able to stop.

quack.meaning: Not real and not honest. A 'quack' medicine is a bad medicine that does not work.

windfall.meaning: A lucky thing that comes without being expected.

clandestinely.meaning: In a secret way, so that nobody knows.

avariciously.meaning: With a very strong wish to get things for yourself.

remorse.meaning: A deep feeling of being sorry for something wrong you did.

numskull.meaning: A person who is not clever.

crestfallen.meaning: Sad because things did not go as you hoped.

forsaken.meaning: Left alone by everyone; with no friends.

succumb.meaning: To give up and accept something you cannot fight.

hermit.meaning: A person who lives alone, away from other people, often for religious reasons.

rendezvous.meaning: A place where people agree to meet.

countersign.meaning: A secret word that you must say to be allowed to pass.

smouldering.meaning: Giving off smoke, but with little or no fire.

waif.meaning: A child with no home, who has nobody to care for him.

sullied.meaning: Made less good; made to look bad.

sweetmeat.meaning: A sweet food, like fruit with sugar on it.

freebooters.meaning: Men on ships who take things from others by force.

obtruded.meaning: Pushed in where it is not wanted.

limpid.meaning: Clear and bright, so you can see through it.

sumptuously.meaning: In a rich and grand way. Here, they eat well.

quicksilver.meaning: A shiny silver metal that is a liquid.

mutiny.meaning: When the people on a ship will not do what the leader says and fight against him.

quartering.meaning: Going across a river in a line that is not straight across but a little up the river.

thwart.meaning: A seat across a small boat.

bereaved.meaning: Having lost a person close to you through death.

ejaculations.meaning: Short, sudden cries or words said out loud.

conjectured.meaning: Guessed from the little that is known.

weltering.meaning: Lying in something and rolling in it. Here, Tom is crying so much that he is all wet with it.

snifter.meaning: A small amount of strong drink or of smoke. It is said that one little bit would be too much for Johnny Miller.

novice.meaning: A person who is new at something.

charily.meaning: With care, because you are not sure.

inundation.meaning: Too much water that covers a place.

hendering.meaning: A country way of saying a word that means to keep someone from doing something.

spume.meaning: White bits on the top of water.

appalling.meaning: Very bad, so that it makes you afraid.

scalped.meaning: Cut the skin and hair from the head of an enemy, as some men did long ago.

soliloquized.meaning: Spoke out loud to herself when alone.

reverent.meaning: Showing deep respect, as in a holy place.

pregnant.meaning: Full of meaning. Here, it means full of signs of what will happen.

funereal.meaning: Sad and slow, like a time when a dead person is put in the ground.

transfixed.meaning: Not able to move, because of a big surprise.

rascalities.meaning: Bad acts that are not honest.

cowhide.meaning: A strong stick or rope made from the skin of an animal. It was used to hit people.

abashed.meaning: Feeling bad about yourself, and not knowing what to do.

slink.meaning: To go away quietly, because you feel bad about yourself.

repentant.meaning: Feeling sorry for what you did wrong.

vivacity.meaning: The quality of being lively and full of energy.

vindictive.meaning: Wanting to hurt someone because of a wrong they did to you.

lacerate.meaning: To hurt deeply. Here, Tom wants to cause Becky pain by his actions with Amy.

prattle.meaning: Quick, silly talk about small things.

artlessly.meaning: In a simple, honest way, with no plan.

humiliated.meaning: Feeling that other people see you as small or silly.

mercury.meaning: In 'a sudden falling of his mercury', a silver liquid in a glass that goes down when it gets cold. Here, Tom's good feeling goes down.

prophesying.meaning: Saying what will happen in the future, as if by a gift from God.

ingenious.meaning: Clever and full of new ideas.

softy.meaning: A person who is too kind and weak.

trounce.meaning: To beat someone hard in a fight.

anatomy.meaning: The study of the parts of the body. Here, the name of the teacher's book.

frontispiece.meaning: A picture at the start of a book, before the title page.

lethargy.meaning: A heavy feeling that makes you want to rest and do nothing.

conned.meaning: Studied and thought about, so that you know it well.

flaying.meaning: A very hard beating. Here, it means the teacher's hard hitting of Tom.

imminence.meaning: The fact that something bad is about to happen very soon.

exacting.meaning: Asking for a lot; hard to please.

retribution.meaning: Bad things that happen to a person because of the wrong he did.

dominie.meaning: A word for a teacher, used in Scotland.

mellow.meaning: Soft and easy; slow and happy. Here, it is because of drink.

gawky.meaning: Tall, and not good at moving.

declamatory.meaning: Like a loud speech that is made to sound big.

unpalatable.meaning: Not nice to hear or to accept.

voluptuous.meaning: Full of nice feelings for the body and the senses.

enhance.meaning: To make something stronger or better.

gilded.meaning: Covered with gold, or with gold colour.

scuttle.meaning: A small hole with a cover, in the top of a room.

regalia.meaning: Special clothes and signs worn by members of a group on important days.

shackles.meaning: Metal rings for the hands or feet. Here, a joke about the promise Tom made.

convalescent.meaning: Getting better slowly after being ill.

relapse.meaning: Becoming ill again after getting better.

minstrel.meaning: In this story, a show with songs and jokes by men who act.

mesmerizer.meaning: A person who puts others in a state like sleep, to show something strange.

phrenologist.meaning: A person who says he can tell what a person is like by feeling the shape of the head.

tract.meaning: A short paper about religion, given to people to read.

incongruous.meaning: Strange because it does not fit with the other things.

discreet.meaning: Careful not to tell secrets or cause trouble.

befriended.meaning: Acted as a friend to someone and helped.

toils.meaning: Nets or ropes used to catch. Here, the law closes round Potter like a net.

deposed.meaning: Told the court, as a promise, what he knows.

foreshadowed.meaning: Gave an early sign of what would come.

delirium.meaning: A wild state of mind in which you do not know what you are doing.

diffident.meaning: Not sure of yourself, and so quiet.

lynch.meaning: To kill a person by a crowd, with no court.

counsel.meaning: A lawyer in a court case.

prosecution.meaning: The lawyers who try to show that a person did a crime.

fickle.meaning: Changing opinions or feelings often, without good reason.

infested.meaning: Was in a place in large numbers, causing trouble.

obliterated.meaning: Taken away completely, so that nothing can be seen.

clue.meaning: A fact or sign that helps to find the answer to a crime.

superabundance.meaning: A much larger amount than is needed.

hieroglyphics.meaning: Pictures and signs used as writing. The boys say the word in their own way.

ciphered.meaning: Worked out as a secret code. Here, the paper must be read slowly to get its meaning.

sepulchral.meaning: Sounding deep and sad, like a voice from under the ground, where the dead are.

berth.meaning: In 'a wide berth', a safe distance away from something.

shroud.meaning: A white cloth used to wrap a dead body.

ha'nted.meaning: A spoken form of a word for a place where ghosts are.

athwart.meaning: Across; from one side to the other.

unkempt.meaning: Not clean and not in order; with bad hair and clothes.

serape.meaning: A bright cloth from Mexico that men wear on the shoulders, like a big cover.

sombrero.meaning: A very wide Mexican cover for the head, with a high top.

milksop.meaning: A weak man who is afraid. It is not a nice word.

swag.meaning: Things that were taken from other people by a bad man.

auspices.meaning: Signs or conditions that show how something will go. 'Under happy auspices' means in good conditions.

gloating.meaning: Being glad in a bad way about something that you have or may get.

sachem.meaning: A chief of a Native American people. The man in the story uses it when he talks big.

debris.meaning: The broken pieces that are left when a thing is broken up.

nobby.meaning: Fine and in good style; very good.

attrition.meaning: The slow wearing down of something. Here, thinking about the events slowly makes them clear.

gunwale.meaning: The top edge of the side of a boat.

flatboat.meaning: A boat with a flat bottom, used on rivers to carry goods.

ostentatious.meaning: Made to be seen by people so that they will think well of it.

sentry.meaning: A guard who watches a place.

auspicious.meaning: Showing good signs for the future; full of hope.

blindfold.meaning: To cover something so that no light comes out. Here, Tom puts a cloth over the light.

lair.meaning: A place where a wild animal or a bad man goes to be safe.

hispy.meaning: A children's game where some boys go away and one looks for them.

chartered.meaning: Paid for, so that you can use it for a special reason.

labyrinth.meaning: A place with many winding paths where it is easy to get lost.

stile.meaning: Steps that let people go over a wall.

sumach.meaning: A tall plant with red fruit that grows on hills.

precarious.meaning: Not safe; it may fall at any time.

quarry.meaning: A big hole in the ground where stone is cut out.

horsewhipped.meaning: Hit with a long thin stick, to hurt a person who did wrong.

vagabond.meaning: A person who goes from place to place and has no home.

posse.meaning: A group of men who are called to help catch a bad man.

embellishment.meaning: An extra thing added to a story, to make it better.

beholden.meaning: Having to say thank you to someone who helped you.

swooned.meaning: Went weak and fell down, not knowing anything.

stupor.meaning: A heavy state in which you cannot think or feel well.

powwow.meaning: A meeting with much talk. The word comes from Native American speech.

constable.meaning: A police officer in a small town.

reverberations.meaning: Sounds that go on and on, coming back many times.

murky.meaning: Dark and hard to see through.

frescoed.meaning: Covered with writing or pictures on a wall. Here, names are on the walls, made with smoke.

sinuous.meaning: Going one way and then the other.

stalactite.meaning: A long stone shape that comes down from the top, in a big hole under the ground.

stalagmite.meaning: A stone shape that grows up from the floor, in a big hole under the ground.

clammy.meaning: Cold and wet, and not nice to touch.

moiety.meaning: A half; a part of something that has been shared.

apathy.meaning: A state of not caring or feeling anything.

fugitive.meaning: A person running away from danger or from the law.

sarcasm.meaning: Words that say the other thing from what you think, said to hurt or laugh at someone.

avocations.meaning: The jobs or work that people do every day.

petitioner.meaning: A person who asks for something in a serious way. Here, he asks God for help.

sheathed.meaning: Covered with a thin piece of metal.

ironically.meaning: In a way that says the other thing from what is true, often to make fun.

oblivion.meaning: The state of being forgotten by everyone.

pardon.meaning: A paper that says a person is free and does not have to pay for what he did.

ransom.meaning: Money paid to free a person who is held prisoner.

pallet.meaning: A simple bed on the floor, made from old covers or dry grass.

orgies.meaning: Parties with too much food, drink and noise. The boy does not know exactly what they are.

lucifer.meaning: In 'lucifer matches', the old name of matches that you light by pulling them across something rough.

waylay.meaning: To wait for people on the road and stop them, to take their things.

slope.meaning: A word that means to go away quickly and secretly.

blowout.meaning: A big, loud party with much food.

effusive.meaning: Showing happiness or thanks in a very strong way.

laudations.meaning: Words that say a person is good.

counterfeit.meaning: Made to look real when it is not. Here, the surprise of the people was not real.

magnanimous.meaning: Kind and good to someone who did wrong to you.

insipid.meaning: With no taste and no interest.

vittles.meaning: A country way to say 'food'. It comes from an older word.

ornery.meaning: A country word that means angry, mean or common.

initiation.meaning: A special act in which a person is made a member of a group.

picturesque.meaning: Pretty and interesting to look at.

refugee.meaning: A person who has run away from a place to be safe.

chronicle.meaning: A story that tells events in the order they happened.

presently.meaning: Soon. It does not mean now.
presently.whyHard: It looks like it means now, but it means soon.

company.whyHard: It is not a business. It means the people around you.

bark.meaning: The hard outside skin of a tree.
bark.whyHard: It is not the sound a dog makes.

pipe.meaning: A small tube used for smoking dried leaves.

fix.meaning: A bad situation that is hard to get out of.
fix.whyHard: It looks like mended, but here it means trouble you are in.

season.meaning: A length of time. With in before it, the phrase means early enough, not too late.
season.whyHard: Here it is a length of time, not spring, summer, autumn, or winter.

custom.meaning: The usual way a group of people does something.

present.meaning: Here, or now. Not a gift.
present.whyHard: It looks like a gift, but here it means here, or now.

lam.whyHard: It looks a little like lamb, but it means to hit.

spare.meaning: To not use something, or to have a little extra to give.

file.meaning: A metal tool with a rough face, for rubbing something smooth.

spell.whyHard: It looks like spelling, but here it is a magic feeling.

thou.meaning: An old word for you, used when speaking to someone.

thee.meaning: An old word for you, used after a verb.

lawn.whyHard: It looks like the grass by a house, but here it is cloth.

latin.meaning: The language of ancient Rome. The school teaches it.

negro.meaning: An old word for a Black person.

mulatto.meaning: An old word for a person with one Black parent and one white parent.

tights.meaning: Clothes that fit tight on the legs.

plume.meaning: A large feather worn as a decoration.

crossbones.meaning: Two bones crossed under a skull on a pirate flag.

jackboots.meaning: Very tall boots that reach the knee.

quarterstaff.meaning: A long wooden pole used as a weapon.

friar.meaning: A religious man who lives a simple life.

crust.meaning: A dry hard piece of bread.

match.meaning: A small stick that starts a fire when you rub it.

bullet.meaning: The small metal piece that a gun shoots.

oar.meaning: A long pole with a flat end, used to row a boat.

kindling.meaning: Small sticks used to start a fire.

chip.meaning: A small piece of cut wood.

breath.meaning: Air going in or out of the body.

conscience.meaning: The feeling inside you that tells you when you have done wrong.

candle.meaning: A stick of wax with a string in it. It burns and gives light.

whiskey.meaning: A strong drink that can make a person drunk.

cupboard.meaning: A closet with shelves, for dishes or food.

bureau.meaning: A chest of drawers for clothes.

loft.meaning: A space under a roof, used for storing things.

broom.meaning: A brush on a long handle, used for sweeping the floor.

basin.meaning: A wide bowl for holding water.

handkerchief.meaning: A small cloth for the face or the nose.

slate.meaning: A small dark board that a child writes on.

circus.meaning: A traveling show with animals, clowns, and tricks.

marble.meaning: A small hard ball used in a children's game.

sword.meaning: A long metal blade used for fighting.

pistol.meaning: A small gun held in one hand.

bowie.meaning: A long knife. The book joins this word to knife with a hyphen.

jail.meaning: A place where a person is locked up.
